ranked.headline: Histology and spatial transcriptomics models recover single-cell molecular states
ranked.summary: Several preprints infer molecular state from H&E or spot-level spatial data, adding per-prediction confidence and correction for transcript contamination.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of single-cell molecular state from tissue measurements. Four preprints treat H&E as a molecular readout. Loki2, trained on 15 million cells, tests how much molecular and cellular state routine histology encodes. GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes and maps senescence across aging mouse organs and human skin. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear morphometric features to spatial transcriptomics. REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence to histology-inferred expression for prognostic analysis in TCGA-BRCA. A second strand improves the reliability of spatial data. st2sc infers single-cell expression from multicellular spots. Dancer separates within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination. SpaceMACE refines tumour calls using spatial proximity. CIRCA recovers identifiable cell and niche programs tied to plaque pathology. A third strand covers representation learning across modalities: Bloom for brain RNA and chromatin, scUNVEIL with next-UMI pretraining on about 92 million cells, scPACE for donor-level states, and GatorAnchor and Elflow for multi-omics and cytometry. A 3D facial-scan diagnostic benchmark falls outside this thread.

ranked.headline: Automation and cross-modal registration scale quantitative cell and tissue mapping
ranked.summary: New preprints pair automated acquisition with multimodal registration, from reusable Patch-seq pipettes to whole-bulb glomerular maps and MALDI-fluorescence fusion.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is scaling quantitative cell characterization through automation and multimodal registration. In Patch-seq, detergent-cleaned reusable pipettes, robotic nucleus extraction and sonication preserve electrophysiology and transcriptomic yield, a stated foundation for automated profiling. Probabilistic C. elegans head-neuron atlases built from near-wild-type strains reach 86.3% top-1 variability-aware identification. Whole-bulb light-sheet expansion microscopy with automated segmentation maps thousands of glomeruli in intact mouse olfactory bulbs. SCOUBI infers axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic transcripts in mouse brain spatial transcriptomics. A second strand fuses imaging modalities: MeXalign coregisters LA-ICP-TOFMS and immunofluorescence via segmentation masks, and FluoMALDI links fluorescence-defined genes, proteins and organelles to spatial lipid composition. Disease- and glia-focused tools add 3D readouts: PASTA resolves amyloid-beta lesion heterogeneity, growth lineages and microglial contacts, and PolyMorph3D quantifies microglia morphology with colocalization of up to four markers. Two methodologically related works fall outside neural tissue: MiSA detects spatial dysbiosis in oral biofilms, and stitched montage cryo-ET maps connected Arp2/3 actin networks in lamellipodia.

ranked.headline: Evolutionary theory shifts from fixed fitness values to structured, context-dependent dynamics
ranked.summary: New models add population structure, plasticity, spatial networks and function-valued traits to coexistence, virulence and fitness-landscape theory.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is theory that replaces fixed fitness values with structure-dependent evolutionary dynamics. A review frames evolution as fitness landscape navigation, relating epistasis, ruggedness and accessibility. Global epistasis models fitted to yeast data predict how fitness in non-home environments changes during adaptation. A multi-locus model shows that mutation rates evolve by indirect selection out of equilibrium and are selected against under homogenising selection. Two preprints extend modern coexistence theory, one by incorporating within-population structure (influenza substrains, perennial plants) and one by adding competition-induced plasticity, which alters niche and fitness differences. Host-parasite models find that degree heterogeneity in spatial networks drives host resistance and spatial variation in parasite infectivity, and that parasite-impaired host mobility favours reduced virulence through changes in relatedness and host density. Formal advances include adaptive dynamics for function-valued life-history traits on Hilbert spaces and continuous stationary distributions of sex allocation at selection-mutation balance.

ranked.headline: Defined protein modules route ROS and H2S chemistry into stress and development outputs
ranked.summary: New apple, pear and Arabidopsis studies pin redox outputs on specific kinases, E3 ligases, transcription factors and splicing regulators.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is redox chemistry acting through defined regulatory modules. In apple, MxMPK4-1 phosphorylates NADP-malic enzyme MxME3-7 at S201, enhancing ROS signaling and iron-deficiency tolerance via malate metabolism. In pear, PUB8 targets ZAT11/12 for degradation, while ZAT11/12 activate LAC1 to drive ROS-linked lignin polymerization and stone cell formation. Two Arabidopsis preprints extend this logic. H2S persulfidation and PRMT5-dependent LSm4 methylation connect H2S signaling to alternative splicing during stomatal closure. Peroxisomal H2O2 homeostasis under PEG-induced water stress rebalances ABA and GA metabolism, slowing germination. Ascorbate control by MdMYB70/MdbHLH62 via MdGGP2 and MdAPX1 in ursolic acid-treated fresh-cut apple is closely related. Less redox-centered are miR159a–BrMYB12 control of myo-inositol/raffinose biosynthesis and thermotolerance, melatonin plus selenium nanoparticles acting via MAPK signaling in salt-stressed soybean, and m6A–metabolome mapping of drought responses in wheat.

ranked.headline: Genomic architecture and contingency decide whether stressed populations adapt or vanish
ranked.summary: New experimental-evolution and introduction studies probe why some populations adapt fast enough to persist while others, despite adaptation, go extinct.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how genetic architecture and contingency determine whether populations adapt quickly enough to persist. In cowpea seed beetles, rapid and repeatable evolutionary rescue on lentil depends on large non-recombining haploblocks on chromosomes 1 and 9. In outdoor Drosophila under insecticide stress, half of the populations went extinct despite strong parallel polygenic adaptation, and pre-adaptation prevented extinction. Replicated stickleback introductions across nine lakes show that source population identity predicts success better than environmental matching. Drosophila suzukii is tested for seasonal adaptive tracking as a driver of invasion. Boechera stricta genome–environment analyses suggest projected hot, dry climates may exceed adaptive capacity. A second strand addresses genetic load: simulations indicate that reproductive competition amplifies purifying selection, and a review links deleterious mutations to crop breeding and conservation. Mosquito models show standing variation evolving against a suppression gene drive and altering its outcomes. What is new is the joint weighing of structural variation, polygenic parallelism, source effects, and the limits of predicting persistence.

ranked.headline: Sequencing workflows are benchmarked and redesigned to control error in assembly, phasing and calling
ranked.summary: Eight preprints benchmark upstream choices and redesign reconstruction steps for assembly, phasing, circular RNA, mtDNA and modification calling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is controlling error at the reconstruction step instead of correcting it downstream. Two benchmarks test upstream choices directly: local assembly consensus strategies for long-read structural variant calling depend on read type and error profile, and polymerase choice affects HiFi assembly contiguity and completeness, with combinations improving results. Method-level designs follow the same logic. GRASER phases short reads on pangenome graph alignments using haplotype-unique edges to reduce reference bias. TERRACE 2.0 pairs outward and chimeric reads for circular RNA assembly. MitoArc adds NUMT-aware filtering and shifted-coordinate processing for mtDNA. NanoHIV-DR yields consensus and read-level resistance profiles, and an inosine model evaluation uses an ADAR-deficient control. Catch*ReSeq targets rare splice isoforms linked to single-cell transcriptomes. Newer here is the pairing of explicit validation controls with these designs.

ranked.headline: Sequence models expand to variant-aware, modification-aware and personalized regulatory prediction
ranked.summary: Eight preprints in November 2026 test sequence-to-function models on variant effects, long-read epigenomes, personal genomes and admixed cohorts.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning for predicting regulatory activity and variant effects from DNA sequence, with attention to where current models fall short. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-specific activity from 1-Mb sequences. ModBERT adds population variants and CpG methylation from long reads, while FiberTron trains a compact model on one sample's Fiber-seq and nanopore RNA-seq. LAMP examines why fine-tuning on personal genomes fails to improve expression prediction, linking this to distal effects, and a comparison in admixed Latino individuals evaluates fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome against variant-based methods. Related single-cell work, including MCT, DRAFT and CMC-VAE, models gene co-regulation, dynamic regulatory networks and causal structure with perturbation prediction.

ranked.headline: Spatially defined senescent niches in aging and diseased liver show distinct epigenetic and transcriptional states
ranked.summary: Three preprints map liver senescence in situ as SenSpots, in human disease and aged mouse, while a p53 study tests a modulator of age-linked liver changes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is spatial resolution of cellular senescence in liver. Human spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq place senescent SenSpots at portal tracts and fibrotic septa, with phenotypes shifting across metabolic liver disease progression. Aged mouse liver multi-omics reports comparable inflammatory SenSpots with distinct epigenetic senotypes and zonation. A causal discovery approach applied to Visium data models causes and effects of senescence markers, which adds an inferential layer to descriptive maps. In aged mouse liver, p53 loss increases inflammation and metabolic damage, and MDM2 inhibitor-driven p53 activation reverses age-linked changes. Human omental adipose is a non-liver comparison, showing more senescence with age than obesity alone explains. Liver injury repair and myocarditis items are peripheral. All evidence is preprint-stage.

ranked.headline: Dopaminergic and cholinergic perturbations reshape striatal projection neuron output across disease models
ranked.summary: Eight preprints link genetic, synuclein and receptor-loss models to altered striatal dopamine release, D1 pathway plasticity and behavioral deficits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is altered dopaminergic and cholinergic control of striatal output in neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative models. Conditional Tshz3 deletion in cholinergic neurons reduces M1 muscarinic transmission onto projection neurons and abolishes D1 versus D2 excitability differences. The 3q29 deletion model shows elevated evoked dorsal striatal dopamine release via PKC-mediated reduction. Functional analysis of 55 SLC6A3 missense variants from psychiatric patients resolves seven phenotypic classes. In 6-OHDA mice, prolonged D1 signaling loss makes direct-pathway neurons hyperresponsive to dopamine. α-Synuclein overexpression in midbrain dopamine neurons produces progressive action-outcome learning deficits, and a human Anxa1-associated dopaminergic population is most depleted in Parkinson's brains. Aralar/AGC1 loss links dopaminergic and redox dysfunction to impaired sociability, rescued by β-hydroxybutyrate. The 5-HT2A deletion study addresses a separate serotonergic and hippocampal axis.

ranked.headline: Perturbation-response models adopt noise-aware, structured designs as cross-dataset concordance proves limited
ranked.summary: Limited cross-source concordance of drug-induced responses and new challenge metrics push perturbation models toward explicit noise and structure handling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that perturbation-response prediction depends on data reliability and evaluation design. A six-resource comparison reports high treated-expression agreement but limited cross-source concordance of drug-induced responses, while the Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 specifies six metrics for zero-shot CRISPRi prediction. Several methods build in noise or structure: DeepCINET models viability assay noise, siGMA applies heteroscedastic uncertainty to noisy cross-dataset siRNA labels, GFM combines knowledge graphs with latent flow matching for unseen Perturb-seq genes, GAIN learns non-additive interactions over an additive baseline, and CIRCE exploits combinatorial perturbation structure to infer graded signaling activity. PTM-BDL extends drug-response prediction to site-resolved phosphosite features. These are preprints, so the reported performance gains remain unreviewed.

ranked.headline: Transcription factors and chromatin marks gate ABA and JA biosynthesis, catabolism and sensitivity
ranked.summary: New papers resolve hormone control to specific promoters, DNA methylation, histone marks and splice events across ABA, JA, cytokinin and auxin pathways.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is regulation of hormone metabolism and sensitivity at defined genomic or transcript targets, with ABA the most frequent node. GhNAC029 represses GhNCED1 in cotton, and RhWUS1 represses RhNCED3 in rose, where cytokinin and auxin factors also act on it. In Brassica, promoter methylation of BraCYP707A3.A02 blocks BraBPC2.A08 binding, linking ABA catabolism to clubroot resistance. In Arabidopsis, SRPKII kinases shape ABA sensitivity via SR45 and HAB1 splicing, and ANAC030 promotes senescence through JA synthesis. Chromatin-level items add context: RSI1/FLD demethylates H3K4me2/3 at its own TSS to limit pathogen-induced expression, and maize H2A.Z mapping links the histone variant to tissue-specific expression. New is the resolution to specific promoters, epigenetic marks and splice events.

ranked.headline: Phenotypic divergence tracks diversification unevenly, shaped by drift, selection, gene flow and niche
ranked.summary: Seven studies test trait evolution against genomic, demographic and ecological parameters, showing phenotype–diversification links vary across lineages.
ranked.synthesis: These studies relate phenotypic divergence to lineage diversification across plants, birds, lizards, butterflies and insects, and report that the relationship is uneven. Mimosa clades span a continuum of diversification rates, with radiations contributing most diversity and disparity and linked to abiotic niche lability. In island kingfishers, faster plumage color evolution tracks faster diversification and accelerates as genomic diversity declines, consistent with drift. Bark anoles show convergent signaling traits decoupled from genomic species boundaries, with gene flow shaping speciation outcomes. Avian iridescent dichromatism is explained by both Darwinian and Wallacean processes, and leaf-footed bug dimorphism is labile. Masked owls and Heliconius cydno add genome-scale evidence of divergence tied to phenotype, island isolation and Andean geography. The shared advance is testing trait evolution directly against genomic and demographic parameters.

ranked.headline: RNA processing and surveillance regulators sustain germline and developmental gene expression programs
ranked.summary: New preprints link RNA solubility, splicing delay and piRNA-dependent transposon silencing to oocyte, embryo and spermatocyte gene expression control.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is post-transcriptional and RNA-centered control of gene expression in germline and early developmental contexts. In zebrafish, fractionation RNA-seq maps RNA insolubility during oocyte-to-embryo transition and links it to ribosome, poly(A) tail and m6A features. In Drosophila spermatocytes, co-transcriptional splicing of Y-loop A transcripts is delayed in a cluster-dependent manner, with delay increasing as cells mature. In mouse germ cells, COPS5 loss lowers piRNA pathway gene expression, reduces pachytene piRNAs, derepresses LINE1 and IAP, and arrests spermatogenesis. Related work covers histone mRNA 3' misprocessing after rRNA biogenesis disruption in C. elegans, exosome surveillance of PROMPTs in mouse embryonic stem cells, Marf1 in the Drosophila accessory gland, and GAR1 in snoRNP-dependent lipid metabolism, extending the theme beyond the germline.

ranked.headline: Higher-resolution genomic and phylogenetic data are reshaping inference in environmental microbiomes
ranked.summary: New long-read, MAG and pangenome work shows that assembly and genomic resolution change ecological inference across sludge, sediment, polar and metagenomic datasets.
ranked.synthesis: The main thread is that resolution of genomic and phylogenetic structure determines ecological interpretation. HiFi long-read metagenomics of activated sludge recovers denitrifiers, nitrifiers and Accumulibacter missed by short-read assemblies, biasing N2O-related inferences. Great Barrier Reef sediments yield 2,698 MAGs, mostly novel, with marked metabolic heterogeneity. The Micromonas polaris pangenome of 14 Arctic strains resolves two cryptic ecotypes and 990 polar-specific genes, and metaEukaryome detects eukaryotic bycatch across 75,727 metagenomes using mitochondrial and plastid sequences. Amplicon-based studies provide coarser context: marble biofilms show taxonomic turnover with conserved phylogenetic structure, English river microeukaryotes track water chemistry, and Florida octocoral microbiomes are host-specific and stable over three years. Systems and methods differ, and only part of the work is genome-resolved.

ranked.headline: Perturbation, spatial and longitudinal assays resolve non-autonomous and isoform-level regulatory responses
ranked.summary: Seven preprints pair perturbation with spatial, longitudinal, chromatin and isoform readouts, plus models of heterogeneity restoration and state transitions.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is measuring regulatory responses to perturbation with higher spatial, temporal or molecular resolution. Perturb-Tags links CRISPR perturbations to single-nucleus expression and accessibility to expose non-autonomous effects, while MolMap profiles chromatin responses to unmodified small molecules in non-crosslinked nuclei. LIFE-seq and LANCE-seq repeatedly sample living tissue, enabling longitudinal spatial transcriptomics of cortical injury and APAP-induced liver injury. FULL-seq jointly profiles accessibility and full-length transcripts, connecting promoter regulation to alternative first exon usage. Two computational works are more distant: models identify mixed feedback networks as most robust for restoring heterogeneity during self-renewal, and a single-cell foundation model (UCE) maps state bridges across 614 states. Together they emphasize within-tissue and within-individual dynamics over endpoint snapshots.

ranked.headline: Open software and benchmarks standardize QC, annotation and statistics across MS omics workflows
ranked.summary: Seven preprints deliver QC, annotation and analysis tools spanning imaging, lipidomics, metabolomics and proteomics, with an emphasis on accessibility.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is the standardization of downstream mass spectrometry data handling rather than new acquisition principles. Several tools are R Shiny apps: LipidRT uses retention time coherence to validate and expand lipid annotations in reversed-phase LC-MS, OSMSS provides no-code differential abundance, phosphosite and enrichment analyses for proteomics, and MetaboRx combines quality metrics with preprocessing for metabolomics. msiFlow 2.0 adds mass recalibration, lipid annotation, batch correction and visual QC to an imaging pipeline. QC Shotgun defines eight relative metrics for benchmarking instrument performance in shotgun lipidomics. MSGFLEX pairs MS-GF+ with XPECTRA XGBoost rescoring to raise peptide and protein identifications in proteomics and metaproteomics. A NanoShield trap column benchmark against PepMap and direct injection addresses low-input proteomics at the hardware-workflow interface.

ranked.headline: Positional and dosage-dependent regulation shapes root, vascular and organ anatomy in grasses
ranked.summary: Wheat and rice root anatomy and stress-linked regulators are now resolved by axis position, allometry, spatial expression and dosage effects.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative control of anatomy in grasses and its functional consequences. In wheat, nodal root anatomy differs by culm position beyond root area scaling, and allometric correction exposes distinct genetic associations. Metaxylem number is remodelled along root axes in wheat and other temperate grasses, with spatial transcriptomics and hydraulic modelling linking vessel patterning to water transport. In rice, OsWOX11 promotes thick AR2 roots and a promoter variant (Hap3) shows higher activity, while an RLC3-KNOX-lignin module governs leaf rolling and drought tolerance. In creeping bentgrass, miR164-NAC dosage separates growth, drought and salt responses via AsNHX1. New here is finer resolution: positional, allometric, spatial and dosage-sensitive analyses. The Arabidopsis NAC38-NAC58-FUS3 seed coat study is a related example of transcriptional control of tissue differentiation.

ranked.headline: Brain function is described as distributed, state-dependent dynamics in low-dimensional configuration spaces
ranked.summary: Seven November preprints model cognition as shifting, low-dimensional network states across rest, tasks and naturalistic viewing, not fixed modules.
ranked.synthesis: The preprints describe brain organization as distributed and state-dependent rather than modular. Structure-function coupling varies with cognitive state, strongest during movie-watching and weakest under working memory load. A meta-analysis of 912 papers finds no single core for self-related processing, only shifting coalitions of systems. Oddball detection in auditory and visual modalities follows shared low-dimensional brain-state dimensions with modality-dependent later trajectories. Resting-state HCP data (994 participants) link spatial and temporal network organization to trait-like dynamics, and a signed dynamic connectivity framework relates subcortical routing modes to network flexibility and behavioral traits. Information decomposition of film-viewing fMRI maps distributed storage, transfer and transformation, and EEG work links sensory representational precision to alpha power, pupil dilation and correlated noise. The common emphasis is on dynamic, low-dimensional state descriptions, frequently derived from naturalistic paradigms.

ranked.headline: SLC25A35 defined as the mitochondrial BCKA carrier, tying substrate import to tissue metabolism
ranked.summary: Two preprints identify SLC25A35 as the mitochondrial branched-chain keto acid carrier, with import shaping hepatic BCKA handling and adipocyte lipogenesis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that mitochondrial substrate entry and organelle remodeling set tissue metabolic output. Two preprints identify SLC25A35 as the mitochondrial carrier for branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs). One also names MCT1 and MCT2 as cellular entry transporters and reports that import limits hepatic BCKA handling; the other links BCKA uptake to adipocyte lipogenesis and fatty acid metabolism. MTCH2 supports mitochondrial remodeling, respiration and fatty acid oxidation in muscle satellite cells. Myeloid mDIC deletion shifts adipose macrophages to an efferocytosis-associated state with preserved respiration. In KPC cachexia mice, muscle OPA1 overexpression or BNIP3 knockdown partly preserved muscle mass and function, sex-dependently. Dual Hadha and Hadhb mRNA delivery restores fatty acid oxidation in a trifunctional protein deficiency model. The new element is the transporter-level account of BCKA import, from cell entry to mitochondrial uptake.

ranked.headline: Cancer studies integrate multi-omic and perturbation data to resolve regulatory and signaling states
ranked.summary: Seven preprints combine transcriptomic, proteomic and perturbation data in tumours, with resources for PDAC and PTM co-variation alongside mechanistic studies.
ranked.synthesis: The current items share a focus on integrating multiple molecular layers to define tumour regulatory states, not on live-tissue or isoform-resolved sampling. Resource-oriented work includes PDAC BioPortal, which unifies bulk, single-nucleus and spatial PDAC cohorts, and PTMlink, which scores glycosylation–phosphorylation co-variation across 1,211 tumour proteomes. A TNBC framework combines Perturb-seq CRISPRi responses with TF binding priors, nominating CTCF, MYC and AP-1 members as master regulators. Serum proteomics with intact N-glycoproteomics, analysed with a DTS strategy, links glycan remodelling to ovarian cancer. Mechanistic and association studies include KDM3B-mediated H3K9me2 removal at the ERBB3 promoter in cholangiocarcinoma, and Mendelian randomization with single-cell data linking midkine to PDAC. A breast–ovarian GEO integration prioritizes hub genes and food-derived compounds.

ranked.headline: Fibroblast matrix-remodelling programmes are mapped across human and mouse fibrosis
ranked.summary: Single-nucleus and cross-organ profiling now resolve matrix-remodelling states in fibrosis, fibroblasts and microglia across species.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the resolution of cell states and the matrix-remodelling programmes they carry, in fibrotic and glial contexts. In human atrial fibrillation, single-nucleus multi-omics identifies fibroblast states, and JMJD1C is proposed as a mediator of TGF-beta-driven fibroblast remodelling. A cross-organ analysis of human and mouse fibrosis RNA-seq data identifies a conserved 25-gene matrix-remodelling core, although gene-level cross-species concordance is weak. The new element is the pairing of single-nucleus resolution with cross-organ and cross-species comparison, and the core remains only weakly concordant between species. Related preprints extend the logic to neural and microglial states: lysosomal MiT/TFE programmes precede and couple to disease-associated microglia reprogramming, and VIP interneurons show the most disrupted synapse programmes in 5xFAD mice. The heart isoform atlas addresses an adjacent question.

ranked.headline: Neuronal proteome and organelle remodelling in neurodegeneration models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints map cell-type-specific and temporal molecular changes in neurons, including TDP-43 interactome shifts and lysosome trafficking control.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how neurons maintain organelle and proteome integrity under cell-type- or stage-specific perturbation. Fmr1-KO profiling reports cell type-specific mRNA and protein remodelling at cortical excitatory and inhibitory synapses, and SETX knockout in human iPSC-derived motor neurons impairs neurite growth, synaptic activity and survival in a stage-dependent manner. A temporal APEX2 atlas of TDP-43 interactomes shows network changes persisting beyond stress granule clearance. Lysosomal quality control is addressed in two items: the axon initial segment is proposed as a lysosome trafficking checkpoint, with MCF2L anchoring lysosomes via gAnkG, and processing bodies promote lysosomal quality and survival during recovery from lysosomal damage. Contact-phagy adds a selective autophagy route that turns over ER-mitochondria contact-site subdomains. The lysosome and contact-site studies are primarily mechanistic and not disease-specific.

ranked.headline: Heat stress combined with other stresses reshapes chromatin, hormone and clock regulation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a proteomics study show plant heat responses depend on stress combinations, priming and circadian timing.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is how plants integrate heat with other stresses through chromatin, hormone and clock regulation. In potato, combined heat and drought alter chromatin accessibility and prime ABA biosynthesis via StNCED3 on repeated exposure. In rice, thermopriming produces a restrained, lower-entropy heat transcriptional response with H3K27me3 retention and memory chaperone expression. In Arabidopsis, combined heat and phosphate starvation yields organ-specific jasmonate changes, with JA-Ile increasing in roots and JA decreasing in shoots. Clock-focused Arabidopsis work links CCA1 and LHY to time-of-day heat responses across transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic layers, while a proteomics study of rve4 6 8 mutants connects clock genes to osmotic and salt stress. The new emphasis is on priming and organ-level divergence under stress combinations; the clock and salt-stress studies address related but distinct contexts.

ranked.headline: Stress triggers organelle turnover via autophagy, tethers and phosphoinositide switches
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers define distinct adaptors, tethers and routes that remodel organelles under starvation, iron deficiency and osmotic stress.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on stress-triggered remodeling of organelles through degradative and membrane-supply routes, mainly autophagy. Lipid and contact-site control appears in yeast, where Mdm1 balances phospholipid and neutral lipid metabolism to allow autophagosome completion, and in HeLa cells, where ATAD1 at mitochondria-ER contacts moves mislocalized Pex26 from mitochondria to the ER. Iron deficiency triggers pexophagy through a GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 interaction that activates TFEB and TFE3. Acinus-induced autophagy requires Rab32 and Lrrk kinase rather than mTor regulation, and RAB11-RAB30 drives endosomal remodeling through a phosphoinositide switch under starvation, shear and osmotic stress. What is new is the assignment of specific adaptors, tethers and signaling routes to each context, rather than a single shared mechanism.

ranked.headline: Elicitor perception and viral effectors shape plant immune outputs across hosts
ranked.summary: Recent reports link systemin perception, elicitor-triggered cell death and antiviral glycosylation to defined immune outputs in plants.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how plants detect elicitors and convert recognition into immune outputs. In Nicotiana, four newly described bioactive systemins are detected by SlSYR1, and a premature stop codon in LAB N. benthamiana SYR1 orthologs is linked to systemin insensitivity. The secreted Ustilaginoidea virens protein UvWSC1 acts as a virulence factor and immune elicitor, triggering OsCPK13- and SOBIR1-dependent cell death. Sugarcane mosaic virus HC-Pro triggers ADR1/NRG1-dependent hypersensitive cell death in N. benthamiana, modulated by P3N-PIPO. In Arabidopsis, UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 restrict turnip mosaic virus independently of salicylic acid, jasmonate and RNA silencing. The mild SCMV maize vector is a methodological tool, and the grapevine NaBut study is applied; both are peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Omics readouts hinge on compartment, composition, donor structure and cell-state context
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that transcriptomic and chromatin readouts depend on cell composition, scoring rules, marker definitions and donor structure.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that omics readouts are conditional on the compartment, cell composition, scoring rule, marker definition and donor structure from which they are drawn. Decoupled transcript scoring of efferocytosis after ischaemic stroke, assessed across 38 datasets, finds clearance signals bounded by cell composition and time. Endometriosis GWAS cell-state prioritization shifts with marker definition, and chromatin accessibility in endometrial biopsies places stromal regulatory context in view. A sequence model conditioned on interferon-beta-stimulated monocyte snapshots predicts the expression response to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects, which defines a boundary on transfer. In cortical GABAergic Patch-seq neurons, channel expression reinforces rather than compensates for dendritic conductance load. Across these preprints, interpretation is tied to the specific context in which each readout was obtained, and the non-coding DNA framework and ImmunoTwin screens extend this view to regulatory and perturbational settings.

ranked.headline: Body-wide microbial coordination and stool-plasma biomarkers track Parkinson disease
ranked.summary: Multisite and stool-plasma profiling in Parkinson cohorts links gut microbial dysbiosis to diagnosis, severity and cognitive impairment.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread in this set is the use of microbial community measurements to characterize Parkinson disease. A preprint profiling stool and plasma biomarkers in 211 Parkinson patients and 204 controls reports microbiome and dysbiosis differences tied to diagnosis and clinical severity. A second preprint profiling five body sites in 150 Parkinson's participants reports weakening cross-site microbial coordination and reduced core taxa across the cognitive impairment spectrum. The new contribution is multisite resolution, extending microbial readouts beyond a single sampling site. Other items address different questions: a multiplexed assay of more than 10,400 GBA1 variants linking glucocerebrosidase function to Gaucher and Parkinson disease, somatic mutation trajectories in ALS motor cortex neurons, multi-omics integration in mouse hippocampus and colon, and ancestral variant analysis. These do not share the microbial focus.

ranked.headline: Omics profiling maps epithelial cell states across pancreatic, cervical and alveolar models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply single-cell, spatial and proteomic profiling to epithelial states in disease and culture models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of single-cell, spatial or proteomic profiling to resolve epithelial and tissue cell states in disease and model systems, rather than a shared mechanism across the six preprints. In chronic pancreatitis, CD73 deletion in metaplastic epithelial cells worsened caerulein-induced fibrosis, immune remodeling and acinar-to-ductal change. Progerin induction in iPSC-derived alveolar epithelial-like cells amplified inflammatory and interferon responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Single-nucleus profiling of paired healthy endocervical and ectocervical samples mapped ten cell types and showed that sampling method shapes epithelial recovery. Spatial transcriptomics of CA19-9-positive pancreatic cancer linked four programs to survival and cell-line drug sensitivity. Proteomics of HGSC monolayer, spheroid and organoid cultures revealed genotype-linked mitochondria-ER contacts and lipid droplet clustering. An integrative analysis identified a 12-gene neuroimmune signature in HPV-associated cervical cancer progression. What is new is the emphasis on how tissue context and culture format alter inferred cell states, though these findings remain preprint observations.

ranked.headline: Early neuronal and glial alterations precede overt pathology in neurodegeneration models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints resolve early synaptic, glial, and metabolic changes in Huntington, tau, TDP-43, and Alzheimer models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is early, cell-type-specific dysfunction in neurons and glia, resolved mainly through proteomic, transcriptomic and metabolic readouts. In R6/1 Huntington's mice, excitatory neurons reduce synaptic proteins before motor onset, while glia show decline in neuronal support proteins. Transgenic minipig putamen shows age-dependent transcriptome and proteome changes at 4 and 8 years. Metabolic studies add astrocytic involvement: deuterium MRS in AAV-induced astrogliosis and APP knock-in mice shows increased astrocytic acetate use, and another study links astrocytes to mitochondrial metabolic alterations in Alzheimer's disease. In tau models, early locus coeruleus tauopathy causes hyperexcitability through reduced potassium currents, and Kv7 activation lowers tau burden. The TDP-43 study extends this framing to lipid overload, linking dysfunction to maladaptive metabolic and cognitive responses to high-fat diet in bvFTD patients and knock-in mice.

ranked.headline: Task-adapted language models extend sequence-only prediction to enzymes and pathogens
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test whether task-adapted protein language models outperform established homology and structure search tools.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is adapting sequence-based representations to a defined prediction task rather than using generic embeddings directly. MicroDUET attaches phylogeny and function adapter heads to a compact genomic model for pathogen surveillance. SMSTPred uses protein language model embeddings to predict SAM-methyltransferase substrate types, and CarmnaDD predicts nitrogenase activity from sequence-derived dual descriptors. S-PLM-TM adds structure awareness to a protein language model to support sequence-only remote homology search. Know Thy Neighbour offers a counterpoint: benchmarking embedding-based retrieval against MMseqs2 and Foldseek, it reports that anisotropy substantially impairs performance. deeprok addresses a related but distinct problem, prokaryotic gene prediction, using a neural network with overlap-aware decoding and reporting fewer errors than Prodigal and GeneMarkS-2. The novelty lies in explicit task conditioning and in direct comparison against established sequence and structure search baselines.

ranked.headline: Somatic mutational processes across normal and chronic-disease tissues
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend somatic mutation mapping to normal tissues, cell-free DNA, and InDel signatures, sharpening mutational process inference.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints, the dominant thread is the resolution at which somatic mutational processes are attributed, ranging from allele-level and sequence-context effects to chromosome-level and indel-level variation. A heterozygous MUTYH carrier shows the oxidative signature SBS18 across multiple normal human tissues, and the DNA language model EAGLE-MUT predicts context-dependent somatic mutation probabilities that vary with sequence context and nucleosome positioning. Chromosome-level instability appears in acral melanoma, where single-cell chromosome counts range from 25 to over 200 and are linked to MMBIR repair. Two cell-free DNA studies extend detection of clonal mosaicism and liver-derived somatic mutations to chronic liver disease and ulcerative colitis without tissue sampling. A genome-wide InDel taxonomy of 887 multiple myeloma genomes adds a distinct class of mutational processes, including a TXNDC5 hotspot and an association with treatment outcome.

ranked.headline: Lattice conformation and MAP factors gate kinesin-1 access to microtubules
ranked.summary: Recent preprints define how lattice compaction, MAP7D1 recognition and a designed miniprotein tune kinesin-1 engagement with microtubules.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how microtubule lattice state and microtubule-associated proteins control kinesin-1 access. A preprint reports that doublecortin compacts lattices through its DC1 domain, stiffening microtubules and inhibiting kinesin-1 and TAT1 binding, based on in vitro and simulation work. Another preprint shows that kinesin-1 preferentially moves along stable microtubules through MAP7D1, which recognizes expanded lattice conformations. A third introduces Sidetrak, a de novo-designed 36-residue miniprotein that binds the kinesin-1 coiled-coil stalk, blocks MAP7 binding and disrupts mitochondrial transport in cells. Together these studies position the kinesin-1 stalk and lattice conformation as regulatory control points. The C. elegans EFA-6 preprint and the ESCRT-III membrane repair study address distinct processes and are not part of this thread.

ranked.headline: Knock-in and knockout models probe SYNGAP1, CASK, dynein and TTC5 defects
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add humanized, inhibitory-neuron and organoid models of SynGAP1, CASK, dynein and TTC5 disorders.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is genetically defined model systems that link specific gene perturbations to neuronal and neurodevelopmental phenotypes. SYNGAP1 c.427C>T knock-in mice, patient iPSC neurons and organoids show reduced SynGAP1 with altered Ras/ERK signaling. CASK deletion in parvalbumin or somatostatin inhibitory neurons produces distinct seizure types tied to different inhibitory synaptic deficits. Patient-derived cortical organoids carrying dynein variants reveal spindle disruption and apoptosis, while Ttc5 knockout mice display brain malformations arising from neurogenesis and mitotic defects, with elevated γ-tubulin. The Drosophila ANKLE2-VRK1 study addresses a related but distinct question: maintenance of proteostasis and neuronal resilience in adult neurons during aging. What is new is the cell-type-resolved or human-derived resolution of several disorder models, and the mechanistic link of TTC5 to γ-tubulin mRNA regulation.

ranked.headline: Penetrance-linked cellular deficits in 22q11.2 deletion models and carrier iPSCs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link variable schizophrenia penetrance in 22q11.2 deletion to neuronal mitophagy, barrier and oligodendrocyte differences.
ranked.synthesis: Three of the six preprints examine 22q11.2 deletion carriers or deletion models, and the dominant thread is cellular compartments associated with variable schizophrenia penetrance. In iPSC-derived neurons from deletion carriers, schizophrenia is associated with impaired mitophagy and lysosomal acidity, a defect described as reversible. In iPSC-derived blood-brain barrier cells from carriers, metabolic and structural differences are linked to penetrance. In a 22q11.2 deletion mouse model, prefrontal oligodendrocyte development is altered, with more immature and mature oligodendrocytes and reduced myelination at P28, although this study does not address penetrance. The new element is the association of penetrance with distinct cellular states across neuronal and barrier compartments, alongside glial changes in a deletion model. The remaining three studies use cntnap2-/- autism, PLX5622 Purkinje cell degeneration and LKB1 granule cell models and are not attributed to the deletion.

ranked.headline: Binding partners and ions are discriminated at defined protein sites
ranked.summary: Six recent preprints map how transporters, disordered regions and integrases recognise ligands, ions and partners at defined sites.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how proteins recognise binding partners and permeant ions at defined sites. Nanobody mapping of the bacterial transporter BasC, combining transport assays, crystallography and AlphaFold3, reveals a preference for the intracellular cavity. Enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics resolves the multimodal landscape by which the FCP1 disordered region folds upon binding Rap74. In the serotonin transporter SERT, Na+ binding at the Na2 site is reported to couple sodium to serotonin transport through TM1, TM5 and TM8 interactions, while XPR1 phosphate selectivity is attributed to direct multi-ion competition in the pore. Three divergent solute-binding proteins share a conserved loss of affinity for perfluorinated ligands, with locally tunable sensitivity to partial fluorination. The HIV-1 integrase study extends this view evolutionarily, indicating that drug-resistance mutations shift folding stability and catalytic geometry only marginally.

ranked.headline: Nanopore and genomic tools resolve species diversity from field and museum samples
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply nanopore sequencing and low-input genotyping to biodiversity inference from museum, field, and minute biological samples.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread in this set is molecular inference of species identity, diversity, and genomic traits from limited or archival material. Nanopore sequencing underpins a barcoding survey of 3,657 European Ulva samples, which identifies 46 species across 30 countries and flags non-indigenous taxa, and a mini-barcoding workflow that recovered COI sequences from 284 of 288 century-old spider museum specimens, adding 53 new BINs to BOLD. Multiple displacement amplification enables WGS and GBS genotyping of single zebra mussel veliger larvae from about 1 ng DNA. Off-target sequencing of 312 spruce bark beetles reveals frequent nematode associates across Europe. A genome size database for 3,539 non-native tetrapods and a reference genome for the Critically Endangered Bermuda skink provide complementary genomic resources. What is new is the extension of these methods to low-input and century-old material.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved and pangenome frameworks resolve allele-specific crop variation
ranked.summary: Long-read, parent-of-origin and pangenome assemblies now show that reference choice alters allele-specific expression and trait interpretation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is that genotype-linked measurements depend on the genetic and reference framework used to interpret them. In heat-stressed tetraploid potato, long-read RNA-seq resolves haplotype-specific expression, identifying a heat-inducible allele and a nucleus-targeted HSP40 isoform. A parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith apple genome shows that matched references reveal sun-exposure and cold-storage responses that other references miss. In Capsicum, a 48-genome super-pangenome reveals structural variation and the genetic basis of carotenoid and capsaicinoid diversity, and a pangenome-guided k-mer GWAS links pungency and aroma terpene traits to Pun1 haplotypes and TPS genes. Switchgrass eQTL and GxE mapping and pearl millet ionomic stability under drought address related questions with less direct reliance on this framework. What is new is the use of haplotype-resolved and pangenome frameworks to resolve allele-specific and reference-dependent variation.

ranked.headline: Germ layer origin and tissue context shape ageing and stromal transcriptional states
ranked.summary: Profiling now separates tissue-resident ageing programmes from systemic trends and tests germ layer origin in ageing.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of multi-layered transcriptomic and chromatin profiling to resolve stromal and tissue-resident cell states, and to ask how origin, tissue context and ageing shape them. Paired bulk, single-nucleus RNA and chromatin accessibility data place healthy human synovium and infrapatellar fat pad stromal cells on a continuous state landscape. In human stromal clones, HIPPO competency signatures and oxidative metabolism are linked to bone-forming potential and osteogenic responsiveness. Across ages, mouse cochlear single-nucleus data show weak concordance with systemic ageing, with macrophages following a distinct tissue-resident programme. Bulk profiling of 24 GTEx tissues indicates that germ layer origin leaves a small but detectable imprint on transcriptomic ageing, with shared immune programmes across tissues. Bovine mesenchymal cells from umbilical cord and adipose tissue show shared and context-dependent adaptations across culture systems, relevant to cultivated meat. All five items are preprints.

ranked.headline: Feedback and practice reshape muscle activation across human and rodent studies
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a 2026 study test how visual feedback, practice and mechanical loading modulate muscle activation and afferent signaling.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how muscle activity is reorganized by sensory information, practice and external mechanical loading. In 14 healthy adults, real-time augmented-reality biofeedback of quadriceps HDsEMG activity shifted activation laterally and increased endurance during dynamic knee extensions. In older adults, split-belt walking practice produced smaller reductions in reactive muscle activity than in younger adults, whereas context-specific muscle patterns were retained. In anesthetized rats, parallel exoskeleton-like springs altered muscle fascicle dynamics and force without changing primary muscle spindle firing, suggesting that mechanical modulation of the muscle-tendon unit can dissociate from afferent output. The items differ in species and paradigm, so the shared theme is methodological: spatially resolved, context-dependent readouts of muscle activation.

ranked.headline: Human iPSC microglia and macrophages reveal distinct inflammatory and HIV responses
ranked.summary: Arrayed Perturb-seq and syngeneic iPSC models now allow direct testing of microglial state regulation and immune cell trafficking.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a focus on human stem cell-derived or single-cell-resolved models of immune cell states. Two studies address microglia directly. An arrayed Perturb-seq platform using the TF-iMG model maps microglial state regulation and target identification. A syngeneic iPSC comparison shows that microglia-like and CAM-like macrophages differ in TLR-driven NF-kB responses, HIV permissiveness and responses to cART. CellVADIS addresses a different scale, applying optimal transport to single-cell snapshots across tissues to infer immune cell trafficking, tissue entry points and T cell homing signatures. Its inferences are computational and extend the same cell-type-resolved logic to cross-tissue movement. The advance across these items is the pairing of controlled human cellular models with perturbational or inferential readouts of glial and immune cell state.
